neighbours.label: a list, not one pattern: 'Cochrane Database', and ' detector' / ' film' as the thing an imaging beam (electrons, x-rays) lands on
fire: The review appeared in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2015.
Smith J. Exercise for depression. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2012.
The electron microscope uses a detector to reveal where each electron lands.
The scanner sends x-rays through the chest and onto a detector behind the patient.
The x-ray beam passes through the hand and onto film, leaving an image of the bones.
Older machines exposed the image onto film, which had to be developed.
A protocol was registered in the Cochrane Database before the trial began.
Instead of an eyepiece, the instrument relies on a detector to record the scattered electrons.
quiet: The review appeared in the British Journal of General Practice in 2015.
Smith J. Exercise for depression. Lancet Psychiatry. 2012.
The light microscope uses a mirror to direct light onto the slide.
The nurse sends the patient through the door and onto a bed by the window.
The doctor looked at the hand and asked about the pain in the bones.
Older machines printed the report on paper, which had to be filed.
A protocol was registered with the ethics board before the trial began.
A smoke alarm in the hallway woke the family in the night.

notes: Probes: microscope 'detector to record which electrons' 0.79, x-ray 'onto film' 0.56, 'Cochrane Database' 0.46, 'Cochrane Library' 0.29; but smoke detector 0.00, particle detector in a tunnel 0.07, 'held the film up' 0.15, PubMed database 0.06, security camera 0.03, and 'detection bias' (the card's top example) 0.03. The opposite pole fires on systematic-review vocabulary (meta-analysis, randomized), so both poles live in the evidence-review register; I could not name what joins the imaging items to it.
